_comment: Hand-curated extra answers. Two reasons an entry appears here:
1. A USCIS bracketed note declares further acceptable answers in prose.
The import script REFUSES to machine-parse an 'Also acceptable are ...'
note and fails the build unless the question appears here. Mis-reading
such a note would silently reject answers USCIS accepts, and that failure
would be invisible -- it looks like the user simply got it wrong.
2. A one-word alternative name inside parentheses. The importer only treats
a parenthetical as a standalone answer when it is a multi-word phrase or
a number, because single bare words are almost always modifiers -- the
'(congressional)' in 'Citizens in their (congressional) district' must not
become an answer. The handful of genuine one-word alternatives are listed
here instead, where a reviewer can see them.
Each entry records what it was derived from.

48.note: USCIS prints 'Secretary of War (Defense)'. The department is commonly called Defense and an officer accepts either name.

59.note: USCIS prints 'Provide protection (police)'. Answering just 'police' names the state power.

118.note: USCIS prints 'Integrated circuit (IC)'. IC is the ordinary abbreviation.

120.note: Also acceptable are New Jersey, near New York City, and on the Hudson (River).

126.note: Eight of the eleven national holidays are printed ending in 'Day'. People routinely name them without it, and Independence Day is most often called the Fourth of July. An officer accepts these.
